text:
Maya L.: Quick check — our replay vs synth roundtrips are diverging on the 8k prompt set. Replay yields 232ms median per token, synth 180ms. Also token outputs differ around stop sequences.
Sam T.: :eyes: do you have a reproducer? my hunch is kernel selection + cold KV paths.
Maya L.: Putting a minimal harness segment:
```
harness: replay
batcher: autobatcher
kernels: [quantized, fp16_fallback]
kv_warmup: false
tokenizer_normalize: true
decode: {temperature:0.0, top_k:50}
```
Sam T.: two suspects: (1) the runtime took fallback kernels for odd seq lengths, (2) KV cache wasn't warmed for replay because timestamps differ. fallback adds ~30–50ms on some steps.
Ryan C.: profiling snippet (samples):
- decode: 120ms
- kv_lookup cold: 45ms
- kernel_fallback overhead: 38ms
Full trace: https://internal/bench/3001
Katie P.: Also saw tokenizer offset mismatch causing extra tokens when stop seq contains non-breaking spaces. That forces different decode loops.
Maya L.: ugh — tokenizer issue + kernel fallback explains both perf and token diffs. any quick mitigations?
Sam T.: try forcing kernel pinning in harness for parity:
`--preferred-kernel=quantized --disable-fallback` and enable kv_warmup true.
Lee S.: +1 for pinning during apples-to-apples. Also set batcher to fixed-size synthetic runs: `--batch-size=16 --pad=false` so we don't hide batching heuristics.
BenchBot: automated run completed: 3001234570 — replay-pin-kernel vs synth-fixed: median 182ms vs 179ms, token mismatch dropped from 3.2% -> 0.1% :thumbsup: 
Ryan C.: note: pinning exposes a regression in the quantized kernel for long-prefixes — seeing +12ms at seq>2048. filing perf ticket.
Maya L.: ticket sounds good. I'll re-run full 10k prompt sweep with pinning + kv_warmup and attach diffs.
DeployBot: FYI rolling a tiny runtime patch to enable `kv_warmup=true` in test clusters at 3001234575.
Maya L.: thanks everyone. plan: (1) rerun with pinned kernel + kv warmup, (2) update tokenizer normalization tests, (3) file quantized long-prefix perf ticket. I'll post full results here.
Sam T.: sounds good — ping me if you want a quick script to toggle kernel pins.
